title: What a day's profit is actually made of
target: Where profit in Supermarket Simulator comes from: market cost, the price you display, the margin behind it, discounts, offers, expenses and the day's record.
version: 1.6.0 (223), read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A shop with at least one product stocked and priced
The pricing side of the shop reachable
A finished day, or the day's results screen open

steps.do: Start from the cost the market tracks, not from the number on the shelf.
steps.because: the market keeps a product cost and a displayed price as separate values, so the two can move apart without you changing a tag (LocalMarketProductCost, LocalMarketProductPriceDisplay)

steps.do: Treat the displayed price as a decision of its own, made on the pricing screen rather than copied from the cost.
steps.because: prices are set on a canvas of their own through a price manager and evaluated by a manager of their own before a change is announced (SettingPriceCanvas, PriceManager, PriceEvaluationManager, PriceChangeNotification)

steps.do: Use the margin the pricing screen computes instead of working it out from memory.
steps.because: the screen computes the margins it needs through a delegate of its own (ComputeRequiredMarginsDelegate)

steps.do: Count a discount against what you receive, not as a different shelf price.
steps.because: discounts are a separate system with their own panel, current discount and rate (DiscountManager, DiscountPanel, currentDiscount, discountRate)

steps.do: Count a wholesale offer against what you pay for stock, not as extra profit.
steps.because: offers run through their own manager, carry a kind and a time limit, and are accepted rather than applied automatically (WholeSaleManager, OfferType, offertime, CanAcceptOffer, isBuyOffer)

steps.do: Check whether buying in bulk actually lowered the unit cost before you count the saving.
steps.because: bulk buying carries a discount ratio of its own rather than being free of cost (bulkDiscountRatio)

steps.do: Expect some goods to reprice themselves, and read the new price before you judge the margin.
steps.because: there is a kind of product whose price is dynamic rather than fixed (DynamicPriceProduct)

steps.do: Read the day's profit from the day's own record, not from the amount of money in the till.
steps.because: the game tracks a daily profit and keeps a daily record, a manager and a screen of its own for it (dailyProfit, DailyStatisticsData, DailyStatisticsManager, DailyStatisticsScreen)

steps.do: Take the shop's running costs and any automatically paid bills off the day before you call the rest profit.
steps.because: recurring costs are a system of their own with types and records, and bills can be settled automatically through their own manager and canvas (ExpensesManager, ExpenseType, ExpensesData, AutoPaymentManager, AutoPaidBillsCanvas, BillItem)

steps.do: Keep borrowed money out of the profit figure and plan for the repayment that follows it.
steps.because: a loan carries a status and its own payments tab, a repayment keeps a remaining payment count, and automatic payments record how they were made (LoanStatus, LoanPaymentsTab, LoanRepaymentItem, remainingPaymentNumber, AutoPaymentManager, paymentViaCreditCard)

commonMistakes: Reading the till total as profit instead of reading the day's own record.
Counting a discount as if it changed the cost of the stock.
Treating a wholesale offer as earnings rather than as a cheaper purchase.
Calling the day's takings profit before the running costs and bills come out.
Counting borrowed money as a good day's trading.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
